gaps.fact: The minimum Grenache shares of the southern appellations (30 per cent in Côtes du Rhône red, half in Côtes du Rhône Villages, with Syrah and Mourvèdre at a fifth) are stated once in the article's tiers and asked in no question.

Picpoul as a southern Rhône white (the Court lists it with Bourboulenc and Clairette for Châteauneuf): no chapter or article names it among the southern whites; in the Rhône it appears only as a wrong option in i-vstj1uuh and as a clause in the explanation of i-za5ja7ux, where its colour forms swell the Châteauneuf count, and otherwise only in the Languedoc as Picpoul de Pinet.

The Court's three pairing points, meaty dishes with herbs, bacon and peppercorn, weight matched from Côtes du Rhône up to Châteauneuf, and white Rhône as the Chardonnay alternative: the article pairs each style, but no question of either bank pairs a Rhône wine by name or offers Marsanne and Viognier against Chardonnay.
Modern southern plantings on trellis rather than as bush vines, a choice the Court says economics dictates: the article has Syrah on wires and nothing on why.

The river's two effects as the Court states them, reflecting light and concentrating the mistral on the northern slopes, cooling the gentler southern ground: the article gives the mistral and the terraces but not the river's reflected light or its cooling in the south.

errors.where: js/data-primers.js, PRIMERS cat Rhône, fact 4 (The southern ladder): "then the crus: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Vinsobres, Rasteau, Cairanne, Beaumes-de-Venise, Lirac and Tavel."
errors.claim: The southern Rhône has nine crus, given as a complete list.
errors.correction: Laudun was raised from Côtes du Rhône Villages to cru by the INAO in September 2024, for red and white from the 2024 vintage, so the southern crus are ten: add Laudun after Tavel (or Lirac). The region article (law, classification and tiers; places; exam) already counts ten and names Laudun, so the Village chapter contradicts its own article. The Court's 8.2023 list predates the change and is not altered.
errors.source: Decanter, Laudun becomes the 18th cru of the Rhône Valley (2024, cited in the article's own sources); The Drinks Business and Harpers, September 2024.

courtUpdates.now: Laudun, on the west bank in the Gard, was raised from Côtes du Rhône Villages to cru by the INAO on 11 September 2024 for red and white from the 2024 vintage (no rosé), the first promotion since Cairanne (2015 vintage); the southern crus now number ten with Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Gigondas, Vacqueyras, Vinsobres, Rasteau, Cairanne, Beaumes-de-Venise, Lirac and Tavel. The Codex article carries it.
courtUpdates.source: Decanter, Laudun becomes the 18th cru of the Rhône Valley; The Drinks Business, Côtes du Rhône announces new cru (September 2024); Harpers, Laudun becomes new Côtes du Rhône Cru.

courtUpdates.now: Gigondas makes white as well as red and rosé from the 2023 vintage, Clairette at least 70 per cent of the blend, approved by the INAO in September 2022; the Codex article carries it.
courtUpdates.source: INAO, cahier des charges Gigondas as modified in 2022 (the article's own source list; no search spent on it).

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 59 (Rhône), Village 33 (Rhône), 92 in all. Beyond the map, Geography & Maps places Lyon in two stems, Producers & Icons asks all five of the Court's producers and Food & Pairing has a peppery red and a cool rosé with no Rhône name on them. Both columns are strongly served on the crus, the grape rules, the soils, the ladder and the Vins Doux Naturels; the thin cells are the Grenache minimums, Picpoul and the pairings. One error: the Village chapter's fact 4 gives the southern crus as a complete list of nine and lacks Laudun, which the article already carries. Otherwise the co-fermentation ceilings (20, 15, 15, 10, none), the 12.5 per cent floor, Gigondas 1971, Vacqueyras 1990, Vinsobres 2006, Rasteau 2010, Cairanne 2015 and the 5 to 10 per cent mutage dose all hold. One search spent, on Laudun; the Gigondas white is taken from the article's dated source.
